plan: 1 Kings 3:16-28; 1 Kings 5:1-18; 2 Chronicles 2:1-18; 1 Kings 6:1-13; 2 Chronicles 3:1-14; 1 Kings 6:14-38

readings.title: Shelomoh's Request at Gib‛on
readings.subtitle: The Dream and the Promise
readings.text: [1 Kings 3:1] And Shelomoh joined in marriage with <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, and took <dn>את</dn> the daughter of Pharaoh, and brought her to the City of Daviḏ until he had completed building <dn>את</dn> his own house, and <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the wall all around Yerushalayim. [2] Only, the people slaughtered at the high places, for a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not been built until those days. [3] And Shelomoh loved <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, walking in the laws of his father Daviḏ, except that he slaughtered and burned incense at the high places. [4] And the sovereign went to Gib‛on to slaughter there, for that was the great high place. Shelomoh offered a thousand ascending offerings on that slaughter-place. [5] At Gib‛on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh in a dream by night, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Ask what <dn>I</dn> should give you.”</dq> [6] And Shelomoh said, “You have shown great loving-commitment to Your servant Daviḏ my father, as he walked before You in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with You. And You have guarded for him <dn>את</dn> this great loving-commitment, and did give him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day. [7] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, You have set up <dn>את</dn> Your servant to reign instead of my father Daviḏ. But I am a little child, I do not know how to go out or to come in. [8] “And Your servant is in the midst of Your people whom You have chosen, a great people, too numerous to be numbered or counted. [9] “Shall You then give to Your servant an understanding heart to rule <dn>את</dn> Your people, to discern between good and evil? For who is able to rule <dn>את</dn> this great people of Yours?” [10] And the word was good in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Shelomoh had asked <dn>את</dn> this. [11] So <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Because you have asked <dn>את</dn> this, and have not asked long life for yourself, nor have asked riches for yourself, nor have asked <dn>את</dn> the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself discernment to understand right-ruling,</dq> [12] <dq>see, <dn>I</dn> shall do according to your words. See, <dn>I</dn> shall give you a wise and understanding heart, so that there was none like you before you, and none like you shall arise after you.</dq> [13] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall also give you <dn>את</dn> what you have not asked: both riches and esteem, so that there shall not be anyone like you among the sovereigns all your days.</dq> [14] <dq>“And if you walk in <dn>My</dn> ways, to guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> commands, as your father Daviḏ walked, then <dn>I</dn> shall prolong <dn>את</dn> your days.”</dq> [15] And Shelomoh awoke, and see, it was a dream! And he came into Yerushalayim and stood before the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and offered up ascending offerings and made peace offerings. And he made a feast for all his servants.

readings.title: The Two Women and the Living Child
readings.subtitle: A Right-Ruling of Compassion
readings.text: [1 Kings 3:16] Then two women, whores, came to the sovereign, and stood before him. [17] And one woman said, “O my master, this woman and I dwell in the same house. And I gave birth while she was in the house. [18] “And it came to be, the third day after I had given birth, that this woman also gave birth. And we were together. There was no one else with us in the house, only the two of us in the house. [19] “Then this woman’s son died in the night, because she lay on him. [20] “And she rose up in the middle of the night and took <dn>את</dn> my son from my side, while your female servant slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid <dn>את</dn> her dead child in my bosom. [21] “And I rose up in the morning to nurse <dn>את</dn> my son and saw he was dead. But I looked at him closely in the morning, and saw he was not my son whom I had borne.” [22] And the other woman said, “No! But the living one is my son, and the dead one is your son.” And the first woman said, “No! For the dead one is your son, and the living one is my son.” And they spoke before the sovereign. [23] And the sovereign said, “The one says, ‘This is my son, who lives, and your son is the dead one,’ while the other says, ‘No! For your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’ ” [24] And the sovereign said, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought <dn>את</dn> a sword before the sovereign. [25] And the sovereign said, “Divide <dn>את</dn> the living child in two, and give <dn>את</dn> half to one, and <dn>את</dn> half to the other.” [26] And the woman whose son was living spoke to the sovereign, for she was overcome with compassion for her son. And she said, “O my master, give her <dn>את</dn> the living child, and by no means kill him!” But the other said, “Let him be neither mine nor yours, but divide him.” [27] And the sovereign answered and said, “Give the first woman <dn>את</dn> the living child, and by no means kill him – she is his mother.” [28] And all Yisra’ěl heard of <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling which the sovereign had rendered. And they feared the sovereign, for they saw that the wisdom of <dn>Elohim</dn> was in him to do right-ruling.

readings.title: The Covenant with Ḥiram
readings.subtitle: Timber from Leḇanon
readings.text: [1 Kings 5:1] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent <dn>את</dn> his servants to Shelomoh, because he heard that they had anointed him sovereign in place of his father, for Ḥiram had always loved Daviḏ. [2] And Shelomoh sent to Ḥiram, saying, [3] “You know <dn>את</dn> my father Daviḏ was unable to build a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> because of the battles which were all around him, until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put them under the soles of his feet. [4] “But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn> has given me rest all around, there is neither adversary nor evil incident. [5] “And see, I intend to build a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to my father Daviḏ, saying, <dq>‘Your son, whom <dn>I</dn> set on your throne in your place, he does build the house for <dn>My</dn> Name.’</dq> [6] “And now, command that they cut down cedars for me from Leḇanon. And let my servants be with your servants, and let me pay you wages for your servants according to whatever you say. For you know there is none among us who knows to cut timber like the Tsiḏonians.” [7] And it came to be, when Ḥiram heard <dn>את</dn> the words of Shelomoh, that he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this day, for <dn>He</dn> has given Daviḏ a wise son over this great people!” [8] And Ḥiram sent to Shelomoh, saying, “I have heard <dn>את</dn> that which you sent me. Let me do <dn>את</dn> all you desire concerning the cedar and cypress logs. [9] “Let my servants bring them down from Leḇanon to the sea, then I put them in rafts by sea to the place you direct me. And I shall spread them out there, then you take them up, while you do <dn>את</dn> my desire by giving food for my household.” [10] And Ḥiram gave Shelomoh cedar and cypress logs – all his desire. [11] And Shelomoh gave Ḥiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty kors of pressed oil. Thus Shelomoh gave to Ḥiram year by year. [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Shelomoh wisdom, as <dn>He</dn> promised him. And there was peace between Ḥiram and Shelomoh, and the two of them made a covenant.

readings.title: The Compulsory Labour Force
readings.subtitle: Hewing Stones for the Foundation
readings.text: [1 Kings 5:13] And Sovereign Shelomoh raised up compulsory labour out of all Yisra’ěl. And the compulsory labour was thirty thousand men. [14] And he sent them to Leḇanon, ten thousand per new moon by courses – they were one new moon in Leḇanon, two new moons at home. And Aḏoniram was over the compulsory labour. [15] And Shelomoh had seventy thousand bearing burdens, and eighty thousand hewing stone in the mountains, [16] besides three thousand three hundred from the chiefs of Shelomoh’s deputies who were over the work, those ruling over the people who laboured in the work. [17] And the sovereign commanded, and they brought large stones, precious stones, to lay the foundation of the House with hewn stones. [18] And Shelomoh’s builders, and Ḥiram’s builders, and the men of Geḇal did hew, and prepared <dn>את</dn> timber and <dn>את</dn> stones to build the House.

readings.title: The Dimensions of the Hěḵal
readings.subtitle: The Side Rooms and Windows
readings.text: [1 Kings 6:1] And it came to be, in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yisra’ěl had come out of the land of Mitsrayim, in the fourth year of the reign of Shelomoh over Yisra’ěl, in the new moon of Ziv, which is the second new moon, that he began to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] And the house which Sovereign Shelomoh built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was sixty cubits long, and twenty wide, and thirty cubits high. [3] And the porch at the front of the Hěḵal of the House was twenty cubits long, according to the breadth of the House, and its width ten cubits, from the front of the House. [4] And he made for the House windows with narrowed frames. [5] And against the wall of the House he built rooms all around, against the walls of the House, all around the Hěḵal and the Speaking Place. Thus he made side rooms all around. [6] The lowest side room was five cubits wide, and the middle one was six cubits wide, and the third one was seven cubits wide; for he made narrow ledges around the outside of the House, so as not to lay hold on the walls of the House. [7] And the House, when it was being built, was built with finished stone made ready beforehand, so that no hammer or chisel or any iron tool was heard in the House while it was being built. [8] The doorway for the middle side room was on the right side of the House. And they went up by stairs to the middle side rooms, and from the middle to the third. [9] So he built <dn>את</dn> the House and completed it, and he panelled <dn>את</dn> the House with beams and boards of cedar. [10] And he built <dn>את</dn> the side rooms of the structure against all the House, each five cubits high, and they were fastened to <dn>את</dn> the House with cedar beams.

readings.title: The Word of the Creator
readings.subtitle: The Promise of the Dwelling Place
readings.text: [1 Kings 6:11] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shelomoh, saying, [12] <dq>“This House which you are building – if you walk in <dn>My</dn> laws, and do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and shall guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> commands and walk in them, then <dn>I</dn> shall confirm <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> word with <dn>את</dn> you, which <dn>I</dn> spoke to your father Daviḏ,</dq> [13] <dq>and shall dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl, and not forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl.”</dq> [14] So Shelomoh built <dn>את</dn> the House and completed it.

readings.title: The Interior of the House
readings.subtitle: The Speaking Place and the Gold
readings.text: [1 Kings 6:15] And he built <dn>את</dn> the walls of the House inside with cedar boards, from the floor of the House to the ceiling he panelled them on the inside with wood, and covered <dn>את</dn> the floor of the House with planks of cypress. [16] And he built <dn>את</dn> twenty cubits at the rear of the House, from floor to the walls, with cedar boards. And he built it inside as the Speaking Place, as the Most Set-apart Place. [17] And the House was forty cubits, it is the Hěḵal before it. [18] And the cedar for the House inside was carved with ornaments and open flowers; all was cedar, not a stone was seen. [19] And he prepared the Speaking Place in the midst of the House, to place <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> there. [20] And the front of the Speaking Place was twenty cubits long, and twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. And he overlaid it with refined gold, and overlaid the slaughter-place of cedar. [21] And Shelomoh overlaid <dn>את</dn> the inside of the House with refined gold, and made gold chains pass over the front of the Speaking Place, and overlaid it with gold. [22] Thus he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the entire House with gold, until the entire House was completed. And <dn>את</dn> the entire slaughter-place that was by the Speaking Place he overlaid with gold.

readings.title: The Keruḇim of Olive Wood
readings.subtitle: Carvings and Overlays
readings.text: [1 Kings 6:23] And inside the Speaking Place he made two keruḇim of olive wood, ten cubits high. [24] And one wing of the keruḇ was five cubits, and the other wing of the keruḇ five cubits – ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other. [25] And the other keruḇ was ten cubits. Both keruḇim were of the same size and shape. [26] The height of one keruḇ was ten cubits, and so was the other keruḇ. [27] And he placed <dn>את</dn> the keruḇim in the midst of the inner house. And they stretched out <dn>את</dn> the wings of the keruḇim so that the wing of the one touched one wall, and the wing of the other keruḇ touched the other wall. And their wings touched each other in the middle of the room. [28] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the keruḇim with gold. [29] And he carved <dn>את</dn> all the walls of the House all around, both inside and outside, with carved figures of keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers. [30] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the floor of the House with gold, inside and outside.

readings.title: The Doors and the Inner Courtyard
readings.subtitle: The Completion of the House
readings.text: [1 Kings 6:31] And for the entrance of the Speaking Place he made doors of olive wood: the lintel, doorposts, a fifth. [32] And the two doors were of olive wood. And he carved on them figures of keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. And he spread <dn>את</dn> the gold on the keruḇim and on the palm trees. [33] And so he made doorposts for the door of the Hěḵal of olive wood – a fourth part. [34] And the two doors were of cypress wood, the two leaves of the one folded, and two leaves of the other door folded. [35] And he carved keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold laid smoothly on the carved work. [36] And he built <dn>את</dn> the inner courtyard with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams. [37] In the fourth year the foundation of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was laid, in the month Ziv. [38] And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, the eighth new moon, the house was completed in all its matters and according to all its plans. Thus he built it for seven years.
